title: Navimower 0.4.7-beta2

## Navimower Schedule: scheduler intent now outranks conflicting MQTT noise

This beta follows field evidence from an H215 Custom queue run where Navimower Schedule had already completed the previous slot and dispatched the next zone, but one conflicting MQTT zone value caused the scheduler to abandon the round.

The scheduler now treats its own deterministic queue decision as the plan owner:

- matching fresh MQTT work-target evidence may confirm a requested zone quickly;
- matching fresh private-cloud work-target / active-zone evidence may also confirm the requested zone;
- conflicting telemetry keeps the start pending instead of suspending the whole Schedule window;
- raw cached MQTT location values are no longer reclassified as fresh target evidence merely because a newer pose packet arrived;
- `currentMowBoundary` is no longer used as wrong-target evidence. It represents the current/physical mowing partition and may legitimately remain on the previous zone while the mower travels toward the newly requested zone;
- unresolved starts remain bounded by the existing managed dispatch/retry safety layer.

The intent is asymmetric arbitration: MQTT remains the fast observation layer, but it does not get a veto over a queue plan that the managed scheduler already owns.

## Custom Area: MQTT-first private-cloud fallback

Custom Area occupancy no longer becomes unavailable immediately when the MQTT pose stream is temporarily missing.

- fresh MQTT X/Y remains the preferred low-latency source;
- sufficiently fresh private-cloud mower-local X/Y may keep the Custom Area sensor available;
- a cloud-backed entry into the area is accepted immediately, which allows gate-arrival automations to open the gate without waiting for MQTT recovery;
- leaving an already-active Custom Area on cloud fallback requires two distinct fresh vendor position reports before the sensor turns Off;
- stale private-cloud coordinates still produce no occupancy decision.

This applies the same conservative principle already used by physical gate fallback: opening a gate slightly early is safer than closing it on one delayed coordinate.

## Field sequence addressed

The captured run showed:

- Navimower Schedule had selected the next zone and the mower was already in an active task;
- the Custom Area used by the sliding-gate automation stayed unavailable while MQTT pose was absent, even though private-cloud position continued updating physical zone/channel state;
- when MQTT returned, the Custom Area became available and the gate workflow proceeded;
- at effectively the same time, the scheduler consumed conflicting zone telemetry and suspended the managed round.

Both sides are hardened in this beta: the gate-arrival Custom Area can use fresh cloud fallback, and transient/cached MQTT zone data can no longer cancel the scheduler's plan.

## Development raw export

The prerelease-only `navimower.export_raw_data` action remains available unchanged for controlled maintainer field captures. Home Assistant Download diagnostics remains the sanitized public-support path.
